diagnosis.explanation: All three implemented methods are already O(1)-per-step recurrent architectures (each processes one event with constant-size state update); none require re-scanning growing history. The pre-registered H3 hypothesis implicitly assumed a comparison against a method whose cost grows with context length beyond O(L) (e.g., a full-attention Transformer with a growing KV cache, O(L) or O(L^2) per query). No such baseline was included in this pilot (a disclosed CPU-feasibility scope decision, see PREREGISTRATION.md). Against the three baselines actually implemented, CACE shows no asymptotic compute advantage: all three scale linearly in total wall-clock time with sequence length, with CACE (0.22-0.27ms/event) roughly 2.3x SLOWER per event than the linear SSM (0.095-0.097ms/event) and faster than the Neural CDE (0.46-0.48ms/event, reflecting its multi-substep RK integration).
diagnosis.lesson: H3 was under-specified relative to the actual baseline set chosen. A properly falsifiable version of this hypothesis requires a baseline whose per-query cost is NOT already O(1) in context length (e.g., full self-attention), which is listed as required future work rather than retrofitted here.
